reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses hysteresis loops and coercivity in mechanically alloyed FeCoNiMnAl powders, not FeMnNiGeSi films, and does not address surface defects, passivation, or cap layers. The key premises linking surface defects to hysteresis and the effect of an Al₂O₃ cap are unsupported by the provided passage.
premises: Surface defects in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films act as domain-wall pinning sites.
Passivating surface defects reduces domain-wall pinning and hysteresis.
A ~5 nm Al₂O₃ cap layer can effectively passivate surface defects on these films.
Reduced hysteresis in capped films will be observable in low-field magnetocaloric cycles.
